Considered one of the greatest directors in the history of cinema, Luis Buñuel (Calanda, 1900 – Mexico City, 1983) arrived at the Residencia de Estudiantes (Student Residence) in Madrid in 1917, where he met Federico García Lorca and Salvador Dalí. Alongside Dalí, Buñuel made his film debut with Un Chien Andalou (An Andalusian Dog ), his first film with surrealist undertones. After graduating with a degree in History from the Faculty of Philosophy and Letters in Madrid, he moved to Paris in 1925. There he enrolled at the Film Academy and began working as a production assistant for Jean Epstein.
